National Health Supply Control Tower

Stakeholder brief · Sample snapshot at 31 October 2026

Illustrative findings from deterministic simulated data for 120 fictional facilities. These figures are not official Zambia health statistics and must not be used for operational decisions.

Where support is needed

  • 106 of 120 facilities (88.3%) submitted reports. Reconcile the 14 missing reports before interpreting regional comparisons.
  • 11.5% of facility–tracer records have zero stock. Availability is 88.5/100; this does not mean all tracers are available at that share of facilities.
  • 243 facility–commodity records have less than one month of stock. Review the Drug availability table to prioritize zero-stock records and overdue reports.
  • ORS has the highest sample stockout share (13.3%). Examine facility records before proposing redistribution; national aggregate months of stock can hide local shortages.

Disease burden and consumption

Malaria accounts for the most simulated cases over November 2025–October 2026 (1,006,033). The malaria–ACT facility-month association has R² = 0.976. This association is descriptive; investigate consumption-per-case anomalies and reporting lags before interpreting departures.

Next operational steps

Validate aggregate HMIS and stock extracts, confirm facility identifiers and units, reconcile missing reports, and replace fictional geographic data. Use the linked views to investigate shortages alongside disease trends. The three-month straight-line outlook is a prototype aid without seasonality or uncertainty bounds.

Live ingestion, scheduled refresh, alert delivery and server-enforced roles remain integration work. The downloadable guide defines the data schema, KPI denominators, proposed schedule and limitations.
